title: A Government Orders an AI Model Switched Off
hook: The US government ordered Anthropic to cut off foreign access to two of its top models over national-security fears — so the company shut them off for everyone. A new kind of control over AI.
key_points: A Trump-administration export-control directive told Anthropic to block foreign access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5.
The order covered all foreign nationals — even Anthropic's own employees — so the firm cut access entirely.
Officials reportedly worried a model 'jailbreak' could become a national-security threat.
Reporting ties the move to cybersecurity research from Amazon and talks with the White House.
After two weeks of negotiation, Mythos 5 was let back for select organizations; Fable 5 stayed offline.
By July 2026, the curbs were fully lifted — Fable 5 began a global release across Claude's apps, AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure.
content_html: In mid-June 2026, the US government did something new: it ordered a private AI company to switch off two of its most capable models. Ars Technica reported that, following a Trump-administration export-control directive, Anthropic blocked access to its Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models — and because the order applied to all foreign nationals, including the company's own employees, Anthropic ended up cutting access for every customer rather than trying to police it user by user.
extra_html:
The stated worry, according to reporting, was national security: officials at the Commerce Department feared that a "jailbreak" of a frontier model — coaxing it past its safety limits — could be dangerous in the wrong hands. The Verge, citing the Wall Street Journal, reported that the directive was triggered in part by cybersecurity research from Amazon and conversations between Amazon CEO Andy Jassy and the White House. Whatever the full story, the precedent is the striking part: the most powerful AI models are now being treated like controlled technology — something a government can restrict access to overnight. For anyone trying to understand who really controls AI, this is a vivid answer: not just the labs that build the models, but the governments that can decide who's allowed to use them.

The standoff didn't end cleanly. The Verge reported that, after roughly two weeks of negotiations between Anthropic and the administration, Mythos 5 was allowed back — but only for a select group of organizations — while the public-facing Fable 5 remained offline. The slow, case-by-case resolution underlined the same lesson: access to the most powerful models is now something to be bargained over with the government, not simply switched on by the company that built them.

The story kept moving. By July 1, 2026, Ars Technica and The Verge both reported the restriction was fully lifted: Anthropic said it would begin restoring Fable 5 access globally on its own Claude platforms, and re-enable it on AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure. After weeks of being treated as a national-security bargaining chip, the model came back online everywhere — a reminder that these episodes can resolve as quickly as they start, but the precedent they set (that a government can flip a frontier model on or off) doesn't go away with them.

related.title: Who Controls AI?
related.hook: The most powerful AI models are built by a handful of giant companies, because training them costs a fortune. Who holds that power — and whether 'open' AI can balance it — shapes everything.

related.title: Rules & Regulation
related.hook: AI raced ahead of the law, and governments are now scrambling to catch up. The big debate: how to curb real harms without strangling a genuinely useful technology.

related.title: AI Rivals Unite to Guard Against AI-Aided Bioweapons
related.hook: Fierce competitors in AI set their rivalries aside to ask Congress for tougher rules — so their own tools can't be used to help build biological weapons.

flashcards.prompt: Why did Anthropic cut off all access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5, not just foreign access?

choices.text: The government order covered all foreign nationals, including its own staff, so a clean shut-off was simplest
The models stopped working on their own
Customers asked the company to remove them

flashcards.explanation_html: Reporting says the directive applied to all foreign nationals — even Anthropic employees — so the company blocked the models for everyone to comply.

flashcards.prompt: What does this episode show about who controls powerful AI?
flashcards.back_html: Governments can now treat frontier models like export-controlled technology — ordering a private company to restrict who may use them, on security grounds.

flashcards.prompt: How did the standoff eventually end, as of July 2026?
flashcards.back_html: Fully in Anthropic's favor: the curbs were lifted and Fable 5 began a global release across Claude's own apps and its cloud partners (AWS, Google Cloud, Azure).
